text:
alex: quick sanity check — we've been getting ops noise from clients with big cold-start bursts. proposal: grant a small ephemeral "grace credit" on session creation that expires after N seconds, instead of immediately throttling. thoughts?

maya: +1 on principle, hate blocking UX on first request. what's the abuse risk?

alex: abuse vector is scripted account churn to grab grace credits repeatedly. mitigation idea: tie grace to long-lived session token + rate-limit session creation per org. also detect high churn and degrade to 0 grace.

sam: can we make grace credits charged to a different accounting bucket (soft credits) that don't affect billing but are visible in console? helps ops investigate.

lee: agree. also need clear interface between admission and runtime — admission should return an "admit_mode" enum and a grace_amount. runtime uses admit_mode to decide enqueue vs immediate serve. keep it tiny: {ADMIT_HARD, ADMIT_SOFT, ADMIT_DENY}.

alex: sketch proto: ```proto
message AdmitResponse {
  enum Mode {ADMIT_HARD = 0; ADMIT_SOFT = 1; ADMIT_DENY = 2;}
  Mode mode = 1;
  int32 grace_tokens = 2; // ephemeral, non-billable
  int64 expires_at_unix = 3;
}
```

rachel: ops questions: how do we surface grace usage in console? need per-route and per-org metrics: grace_used, grace_expired, grace_abused_flag. and alerts if grace_abuse_rate > X%.

maya: also think about fairness: if many clients get small grace credits simultaneously, we could still overwhelm backend. suggestion: grace credits are applied after local batching heuristics (so they can be coalesced), and runtime should still enforce a short tail-latency SLO.

sam: tradeoff note: grace reduces immediate user-facing errors but increases risk of stealthy net load. prefer conservative default (e.g., 5 tokens, 3s) and allow per-customer tuning via Dedicated / Enterprise config.

lee: interface boundary: admission service should not own KV-cache lifetimes or batching decisions. it only issues admission tokens and modes. runtime keeps batching, kv cache and quantization decisions. that keeps responsibilities clear.

alex: agreed. also will add a behavioral flag in admit telemetry: "grace_trigger_reason" enum: SESSION_START, RETRY_BACKOFF, LEGACY_CLIENT. helps rule-based tuning.

devops-bot: deploy triggered: admission-service v2.4.1 -> canary to prod (traffic 5%)

rachel: small nit — need a rollout plan: start with internal tenants + low-SLA orgs, monitor grace_abuse_rate and cpu spillover. disable for orgs with high churn.

maya: one more: make grace credits non-transferable across regions (so cross-region session recreation can't double-dip).

sam: can we add a fast circuit-breaker telemetry event so SRE can auto-scale if grace causes CPU spikes? e.g., event name: "grace_load_spill" with fields: org_id, region, grace_tokens_used, cpu_pct.

alex: will draft RFC follow-up summarizing: proto change, telemetry fields, default values (5 tokens / 3s), per-org opt-out, rollout plan. will include script to patch admission mocks for integ tests.

lee: LGTM. add explicit auth check: require session token age > 30s for grace unless whitelisted, helps block churn bots.

rachel: can someone add a short doc in Console ops playbook about how to interpret grace metrics? I'll own the alert thresholds. :+1:

alex: thanks — I'll post RFC follow-up and link to a short canary run checklist.

maya: fyi, adding an integration test case: simulate 1k new sessions/min and assert grace_abuse_rate stays < 1%.

sam: ok, schedule sync with SRE tomorrow to agree on thresholds.

alex: thanks everyone.
